newsitem.title: USA: USDA to respond to 'unfair' grain sales - Goldthwait.
newsitem.headline: USDA to respond to 'unfair' grain sales - Goldthwait.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department's sales manager said Tuesday that export subsidies were an important weapon to hold in reserve in case of unfair sales tactics by U.S. competitors in the world grain market.
"I don't think we can make it any clearer," sales manager Chris Goldthwait told reporters.
However, Goldthwait warned against assumptions whether USDA would employ subsidized grain sales this summer.
"I wouldn't make any assumptions one way or another about that," Goldthwait said.
He said U.S. crop development and market conditions would determine whether subsidies were used.

There was rising expectations among private analysts that USDA would begin offering export subsidies in July or August, when this year's wheat crop will be harvested. The United States has not subsidized a grain sale in nearly two years.
Goldthwait was in Brussels last week to meet EU counterparts and to renew U.S. admonitions against unrealistically low sales prices.
Congress allotted $100 million for export subsidies this fiscal year, USDA requested $500 million for fiscal year 1998.
